meaning: The ordered builder steps that recreate the selected body manifest (robot/design.json body_manifest) from the per-section outputs and pinned inputs. Each step reads the previous manifest; some edit it in place. Commands run from the repository root (or from the isolated copy made by robot/body/bom/rebuild_chain.py). Paths are repository-relative. Read by robot/body/bom/rebuild_chain.py and by the BOM tooling.

section_inputs.note: Outputs of the per-section builders (leg, arm, neck-head, torso) that step 1 reads. They are not rebuilt by this chain; the isolated copy links them read-only from the main checkout. Rebuilding them is a separate, earlier chain per section.
section_inputs.copied_writable_note: Section folders that also hold section inputs, but a hook rewrites some of their files (roll_flip_checks manifest -> neck_parts.apply rebuilds the XM335 neck connectors and their screws into neck-head/parts and the sleeves into neck-head/combined). Copied into the copy at setup, so the chain never writes through a link into the main checkout (2026-11-20: 16 neck screw meshes rewritten in main, byte-identical).

steps.notes: Also reads every native_step / mesh named by the section manifests (old artifacts/cove50-strength/... paths resolve through infra/storage/path-moves.json). Compiles robot/electronics/power/cad/zbuffer_renderer.cpp for its renders. Every data output (assembly-parts.json, parts/, bom.json, verification report, manifest.json) is written before the final render phase; on 2026-11-20 the render phase went past 6 GB (peak 6.24) and memguard stopped it after the data was complete. Cap 10 GB for that render phase (peaks 6.24 and 8.22 GB on 2026-11-20), so a chain run does not stop at step 1.
Official ST3025 STEP from artifacts/robot/actuators. robot/body/motor-refit/package.py (GLB, skeleton STEP, renders) is presentation only; no later step reads its outputs, so it is not in the chain.

Env APE_OUT / APE_UPPER / APE_FOREARM / APE_SHELL_PASS only for variants; defaults are the selected build. In Git since 2026-11-20 (Idle T-be4dt7; until then untracked). Code vs the selected outputs: the edits made after the selected assembly-parts.json (2026-11-15 05:07 CET) are the reviewer fixes of T-xdcjn9 / T-gqwdrn (elbow motor sign negated once by elbow_flip.flip_motor_sign, as the selected shell-pass manifest already carries; hip pitch-to-roll volume scaled by the mesh ratio, those parts are replaced by the roll-flip connectors later), and the cradle-cut tool size, now back at the selected 2500 faces / 150 per batch. Stall of 2026-11-20 (past 3600 s, no output after the hip sleeve gmsh line): hips.py's pelvis-cradle cut built one lazy manifold3d CSG tree of 3,538 swept copies and evaluated it in a single to_mesh() call (stack dumps; the gmsh sleeve meshes take under 1 s). Fixed by evaluating per batch (hips.cut_cradle): build.py 264 s, peak 4.3 GB; output equal to the selected step-3 manifest except the cradle mesh triangulation (same surface within 2e-5 mm) and the two reviewer fixes.

Voxel sweep of the hip and ankle target ranges; the script's docstring runs it under memguard --limit-gb 12 (not applied here: the chain runs every step at the memguard default unless a step's limit is approved). shells.py was modified 2026-11-15 06:47, after the selected shell-pass manifest (06:44). 12 GB cap: at 6 GB memguard stopped build.py while gmsh meshed the hip pitch-to-roll sleeves STEP (2026-11-20); shells.py documents 12 GB. Approved by the owner 2026-11-20.
Edited foot monocoque + sleeves (T-rptay5) that roll_flip_checks manifest swaps in; without it the manifest keeps the unedited foot and warns (2026-11-20 run).
Edited hip yaw-to-pitch connector + sleeves (T-v3kzs4) that roll_flip_checks manifest swaps in.

Rebuilt stage 3 torso carrier + sleeves (T-nh6ytf) that roll_flip_checks manifest swaps in; until 2026-11-20 the copy read the main checkout's records through the torso link. Since 2026-11-22 (T-bv7bwe) it also writes the threaded stage-1 interface sleeves, their screws and the stage-1 clearance sleeve part without those positions (from the shell-pass manifest's stage-1 sleeve STEP). Since T-htfaaz it also rebuilds the stage 4 IMU/ADC carrier + its 6 rail sleeves (outer face on the boards, rail sites from common.stage4_rail_sites), the 8 PA2 board screws, and Stage 1 with the bores of the two moved stage 4 rail sites (stage-1 body and its sleeve STEP read from the shell-pass manifest).

Parts nothing held (T-3npyjq): the fan bridge plate + sleeves and the fan's two upper screws re-seated on it, the chest indicator rebuilt to fill its pocket (printed with the front shell), the R roll case's invalid vendor solid rebuilt from its outer shell, the stale r1 front-shell screws and the fan's lower right screw stack dropped; roll_flip_checks manifest swaps them in. Reads the indicator, case and fan sources named by the shell-pass manifest.
New Stage 4 / Stage 5 roll-flip connectors (B-rep) and sleeves; imports the thigh shell's SURF skin from robot/body/leg/thigh_shell.py.

Bootstrap pass: ankle_coupler_screws.py build reads the coupler from this manifest, and this manifest swaps in the coupler that build writes (circular). Without records.json it keeps the unedited coupler and prints a WARNING.
Edits the coupler STEP named by the roll-flip manifest. Not idempotent if that manifest already carries the edited coupler (it would edit the edited part), hence the bootstrap pass before it.
Rewrites the variant from the shell-pass manifest with the edited coupler swapped in and the hip / coupler screws generated from their defined holes.

Replaces the four thigh hard covers with the blue thigh shells (THIGH_SHELL_MANIFEST / THIGH_SHELL_OUT redirect it). Surface parameters SURF are code constants; fit-surface is not part of the rebuild.
Trims the lower leg's back hard cover over KNEE_RANGE and re-mounts it with PA2x8 screws.
Shoulder U connectors and the STS3250 roll idler (B-rep), placed against the roll-flip body. Selected for Shoulder at f5dc4f036 (study shoulder-roll-u-connectors).

Applies the shoulder U connectors to the roll-flip body: per side a roll idler, generated M3x8 x4, M3x6 x4, M2x12 x4; removes the roll case's 4 PA2 and the two upper-arm cover posts with their M3 screws and nuts. body_manifest_chain in robot/design.json.
